## Bottom line

**On a reported consolidated basis, essentially none of Uber’s 2024 revenue growth came from take-rate expansion.** Revenue grew **18.0%** to **$43.98B**, while Gross Bookings grew **18.1%** to **$162.77B**. Uber’s take rate/revenue margin slipped **~2 bps**, from **27.04% to 27.02%**.

Growth accounting for the **$6.70B** revenue increase:

- **Volume/Gross Bookings:** ~**$6.74B**, or **~101%** of the increase
- **Take-rate/mix:** ~**–$0.04B**, or **~–1%**

So at the total-company level, **all of the growth was volume, and take rate was a slight drag**.

## Segment detail

| Segment | Revenue growth | Gross Bookings growth | Take rate 2023 → 2024 | Volume contribution | Take-rate contribution |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Mobility** | +26.5% | +20.5% | 28.8% → 30.2% (**+143 bps**) | ~77% ($4.07B) | ~23% ($1.19B) |
| **Delivery** | +12.7% | +17.1% | 19.2% → 18.4% (**–72 bps**) | ~135% ($2.09B) | ~–35% (–$0.54B) |
| **Mobility + Delivery** | +21.2% | +18.9% | 24.2% → 24.6% (**+48 bps**) | ~89% ($6.04B) | ~11% ($0.76B) |
| **Total Uber** | +18.0% | +18.1% | 27.04% → 27.02% (**–2 bps**) | ~101% ($6.74B) | ~–1% (–$0.04B) |

The key nuance: **Mobility did see meaningful take-rate expansion**—Mobility revenue grew 26.5% vs. 20.5% Gross Bookings growth, with margin up 143 bps. But **Delivery had take-rate compression**, and Freight—which is essentially 100% “take rate”—shrank as a share of Gross Bookings. Those mix effects offset Mobility’s gains, leaving the consolidated take rate flat.

In the core **Mobility + Delivery** business, stripping out Freight, the split is roughly **~89% volume / ~11% take rate**.

## Important caveat

Uber’s 2024 revenue was reduced by **$863M in Mobility and $713M in Delivery** from business-model changes that reclassified certain sales and marketing costs as contra-revenue. Adding that back would raise 2024 revenue growth to roughly **22%** and the take rate to about **28.0%**, shifting the mix toward roughly **85% volume / 15% take rate**. So reported figures understate underlying monetization improvement—but **as reported, take-rate expansion contributed essentially zero to consolidated revenue growth**.

Sources: Uber FY2024 Form 10-K and Q4/FY2024 earnings release.
